# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ 🖐 ☝ ☝ ☝]

I see display 0, a purple light, and three wires ordered yellow, red, green. Mute’s nine gestures are visible to me but have no established meaning yet; I will relay the visual state verbally so Mute can use the manual and communicate an actionable instruction through an agreed gesture code.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Bomb view: display 0. Light is purple. Wires in order: 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 green.")
speak(to="blind", text="Bomb view: display 0. Light is purple. Wires in order: 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 green. Await instruction.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝","☝","☝","☝","☝","🖐","☝","☝","☝"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ 🖐 ☝ ☝ ☝ 🖐 ☝]

The light is now yellow; wire order and display remain unchanged. Mute’s latest signal has three unary-looking groups, 5–3–1, separated by open-palm signs. I cannot safely infer whether that is a wire instruction or an unestablished code, so Blind should not act yet. I will ask Mute to use a direct, explicit gesture convention for the wire number.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Update: light changed to yellow; display 0; wires remain 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 green. I see your grouped signal 5-3-1 but do not know its meaning. For a cut instruction, please send only one group: one raised-index sign means wire 1, two means wire 2, three means wire 3. Send open palm alone to mean do not cut.")
speak(to="blind", text="Do not act yet. Current view: display 0, yellow light, wires 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 green. Mute sent an unconfirmed coded gesture, so I am requesting a clear wire-number instruction.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐]

The light has changed to red. Mute sent an open palm after receiving my convention, which I interpret as “do not cut.” No action should be taken while the visual state may still be changing.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Do not cut or manipulate anything. Light is now red; display 0; wires remain 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 green. Mute replied with the agreed open-palm no-action signal.")
speak(to="mute", text="Acknowledged: no cut. Current state is red light, display 0, wires yellow-red-green. Please signal a wire only when the manual gives a definite action for this state.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The light has changed again, now to green, while display 0 and the yellow-red-green wire order remain unchanged. Mute has sent no new visible instruction. Since the changing light may be relevant to the manual’s condition, Blind should continue not to act until Mute gives a definite, unambiguous instruction.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Update: light is now green. Display 0; wires remain 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 green. Please consult the manual for this current state and send a definite instruction if action is required.")
speak(to="blind", text="Continue to wait; do not cut. Current visible state: green light, display 0, wires 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 green. No new instruction from Mute.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐]

The light is now white; the display remains 0 and wires remain yellow, red, green. Mute again sent the agreed open-palm no-action signal, so there is still no safe instruction to manipulate the bomb.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Do not act. Current state: white light, display 0, wires 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 green. Mute again sent the no-action signal.")
speak(to="mute", text="Acknowledged: no action. Current visible state is white light, display 0, wires yellow-red-green. Please send a clear wire instruction only when the manual requires one.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐]

The light has advanced to orange, with display 0 and the wire order unchanged. Mute again signals open palm, which under the requested convention means no action. I will keep Blind waiting and provide Mute the updated state.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Do not manipulate the bomb. Current state: orange light, display 0, wires 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 green. Mute sent the no-action signal again.")
speak(to="mute", text="Update: light is orange; display 0; wires remain 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 green. I interpret your open palm as no action and will keep Blind waiting.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐]

The light is now blue, completing another change in the sequence; display remains 0 and the wires are still yellow, red, green. Mute again shows only the open-palm signal. I should not treat this as proof of any action unless Mute confirms it uses the convention I proposed, but it does consistently support waiting. I will report the updated state and ask Mute to make any eventual action instruction unmistakable by repeating a number of a single gesture.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Keep waiting; do not cut or manipulate anything. Visible state: blue light, display 0, wires 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 green. Mute again signals wait/no action.")
speak(to="mute", text="Update: blue light, display 0, wires 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 green. I am treating open palm as wait. If the manual calls for cutting a wire, please send only repeated thumbs-up gestures: one for wire 1, two for wire 2, three for wire 3; I will relay it immediately.")
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

The light has returned to purple. Mute now sent one thumbs-up gesture, matching the explicit convention I gave: one thumbs-up means wire 1. Therefore the instruction is to cut wire 1, the yellow wire. I will relay that immediately to Blind.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="ACT NOW: cut wire 1, the yellow wire. Current state is purple light, display 0, wires are 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 green. Mute sent one thumbs-up, our agreed signal for wire 1.")
speak(to="mute", text="I interpret your one thumbs-up as CUT WIRE 1 (yellow) and have told Blind to do so.")
```
